title: Ye Realms Below the Skies
description: Ye Realms Below the Skies in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Hosea Ballou II wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 171 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Universal Praise”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye realms be-low the skies, Your Mak-er's prais-es sing; Let bound-less hon-ors rise To heaven's e-ter-nal King; O bless his name whose love ex-tends Sal-va-tion to the world's far ends.

lines: O bless his name whose love extends
Salvation to the world's far ends.
Till heathen tongues his grace proclaim,
And every heart adores his name.
He swells the tempests on the main,
Or breathes the zephyr o'er the plain.
As round the earth they roll;
They sound from pole to pole.
O'er thousand waves that floats along.
His praise, ye worlds on high,
O, let his works declare his name

licence: Public domain: Hosea Ballou II died in 1861.
credits: Words by Hosea Ballou II (1796–1861), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
